cohort: 594 opioid-naïve patients who underwent non-emergent cesarean delivery (217 primary and 377 repeat).
finding: Opioid-naïve obstetric patients who undergo non-emergent repeat cesarean delivery demonstrate lower opioid consumption in the postoperative period compared to those undergoing primary cesarean delivery.
mod_finding: Opioid-naïve obstetric patients who undergo non-emergent repeat cesarean delivery demonstrate lower opioid consumption in the postoperative period compared to those undergoing primary cesarean delivery.
